series_label: 河西走廊历史阅读 · 连载 06
title_en: The Camels and the Complaint: A Dispute at Xuanquan
title_zh: 骆驼与申诉：悬泉置留下的一场交易争议
lead: 一份来自悬泉置的申诉文书，把驿站的粮草记录带进了一场跨境交易争议。

paragraphs.en: Three white camels became the center of a complaint preserved on seven wooden strips from Xuanquan Station. Envoys acting for Central Asian rulers said that Han officials had valued the animals as less valuable yellow or tan camels. The strips do not give us a scene to watch or a verdict to repeat. They give us a dispute and the official effort to investigate it. Yesterday's article followed names, grain, and messages at Juyan. At Xuanquan, near Dunhuang on the main Hexi route, those routines met travelers whose expectations did not match what they said had happened.
paragraphs.zh: 三峰白骆驼成了一份申诉的焦点；文书保存在悬泉置出土的七枚木简上。代表中亚统治者的使者称，汉朝官员把这些骆驼按价值较低的黄色或褐色骆驼估价。木简没有给我们可目睹的场景，也没有可复述的裁决；它留下的是一场争议，以及官府试图调查的过程。上一篇追踪居延的姓名、粮食与文书递送；在河西主道、敦煌附近的悬泉置，这些日常事务遇上了认为实际待遇与预期不符的行旅。

paragraphs.en: The place matters. Xuanquan was a Han relay station on the route toward the western passes. Excavations in 1990–92 recovered administrative writing from a station used over many generations. Unlike Juyan's northern frontier posts, this was a stopping point on a heavily traveled corridor. Messages moved through it, but so did diplomatic parties and the animals accompanying them. A station could offer transport and provisions, while also keeping records that might later be checked. The surviving archive is incomplete; its value lies in showing how a route worked when travel raised questions that walls and roads alone could not answer.
paragraphs.zh: 地点很重要。悬泉置是通往西部关隘的汉代驿站。1990至1992年的发掘，找到了这座使用多代人的驿站所留下的行政文书。它不同于居延北部的边塞驻地，是繁忙通道上的停驻点。经过这里的不只有消息，还有外交使团和随行牲畜。驿站可以提供交通与给养，也会留下日后可供核查的记录。档案保存并不完整；它的价值在于说明，当行旅提出城墙与道路本身无法回答的问题时，通道如何运作。

paragraphs.en: According to the petition summarized in the Xuanquan manuscript, envoys had previously passed the Dunhuang frontier and traveled at government expense to trade camels at Jiuquan. They expected to take part in assessing the animals' value. On this journey, they alleged, promised provisions did not arrive and the governor excluded them from the assessment. The claimed loss was therefore about more than a price: it involved food, procedure, and whether an agreement was honored. We must keep the source's point of view visible. These are the envoys' allegations, not independent proof that every official acted as accused.
paragraphs.zh: 据悬泉置文书概述的申诉，使者过去曾越过敦煌边关，在官府承担费用的条件下前往酒泉交易骆驼。他们原本预期能参与牲畜估价。这一次，他们称约定的给养没有到位，太守也把他们排除在估价之外。因此，他们所称的损失不只是价钱，还涉及食物、程序，以及约定是否得到履行。必须保留史料的叙述角度：这些是使者的指控，并非每名官员确如所述行事的独立证据。

paragraphs.en: The animal details made the argument concrete. The petition says three white camels sent for the king of Suxie were recorded as yellow or tan. It also says camels associated with the king of Kangju were judged undernourished; the envoys connected that judgment to missing fodder. Color and condition affected the valuation they challenged. The document does not tell us the full earlier journey of either herd, and a modern reader cannot inspect the animals. Yet it shows why care at relay stations mattered to visiting parties. A shortage of feed could become a diplomatic and commercial grievance, not merely an inconvenience along the road.
paragraphs.zh: 牲畜的细节让争议变得具体。申诉称，替苏薤王送来的三峰白骆驼被记作黄色或褐色；又称与康居王有关的骆驼被判为瘦弱，使者把这一判断同缺少饲料联系起来。毛色与体况影响了他们所质疑的估价。文书没有交代两群骆驼此前的完整行程，今天的读者也无法亲自检视牲畜。但它说明驿站的照料为何关系到来访使团：饲料短缺可能成为外交与交易上的申诉，而不只是路途上的不便。

paragraphs.en: The complaint did not simply disappear at a local desk. A study of the Xuanquan records traces its movement to the Han court. In 39 BCE, court-appointed officials requested an investigation; their instruction reached Dunhuang after more than a month and was copied onward through Xiaogu county to Xuanquan. The station was asked to report figures for provisions consumed by the Kangju party within three days. This is a rare view of a long administrative chain running in both directions: a complaint traveled toward the center, and a demand for numbers traveled back toward the place where supplies had been handled.
paragraphs.zh: 申诉并未止于地方官署。一项对悬泉文书的研究追踪了它传往汉朝朝廷的过程。公元前39年，朝廷任命的官员要求调查；命令一个多月后到达敦煌，又经效谷县抄送悬泉置。驿站被要求在三天内报送康居使团消耗给养的数目。这让我们罕见地看到一条往返运行的行政链：申诉向中央传递，索取数字的要求则传回处理给养的地点。

paragraphs.en: This return request changes how we read the wooden slips. At Juyan, a grain register showed that issues of food were measured; a post register showed that handovers were dated. At Xuanquan, those same habits became tools for testing a contested account. Officials needed quantities because the envoys said they had not received what was promised. The order to report is evidence of an inquiry, not evidence of its outcome. We do not know from these surviving pieces whether the envoys were compensated or whether the accused officials were punished. A complete story can end with an established process and an honestly unresolved judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 这道回查命令改变了我们阅读木简的方式。居延的粮簿显示食物发放需计量，驿递簿显示交接需记日期；在悬泉置，同样的习惯成了核查争议说法的工具。使者称没有得到约定的给养，官员因此需要核对数量。要求报送的命令证明调查发生，不能证明调查结果。现存材料没有告诉我们使者是否获偿，或被指控的官员是否受罚。一个完整的故事，可以以确有证据的程序和仍未解决的裁断收尾。

paragraphs.en: The petition also complicates a simple picture of one empire controlling a passive road. The visitors represented particular Central Asian rulers and made a formal claim against Han officials. Han offices had power over passage, supplies, and valuation, but their decisions could be challenged and sent upward for review. The exchange mixed state ceremony with practical bargaining over animals and food. The wooden text is an official survival, so it cannot reveal all the voices around the station, including workers who fed horses or camels. Still, it preserves the envoys' challenge inside the very administrative system they disputed.
paragraphs.zh: 这份申诉也让“一个帝国控制一条被动道路”的简单图景站不住脚。来访者代表具体的中亚统治者，并正式向汉朝官员提出异议。汉朝官署掌握通行、给养与估价的权力，但其决定也可能受到质疑，并被上送审查。这场往来既有国家礼仪，也有围绕牲畜与食物的实际协商。木简作为官府文书幸存，无法呈现驿站周围所有人的声音，包括喂养马匹或骆驼的劳作者；但它把使者的质疑保存在他们所质疑的行政体系之内。

paragraphs.en: Xuanquan therefore answers the question left by Juyan with a sharper case. Registers and relays did more than keep a frontier post supplied: they made promises, complaints, and inquiries traceable across the Hexi Corridor. The documented chain did not guarantee fairness. It gave people a way to contest an account and officials a way to demand evidence. We can state that much without inventing a favorable verdict. For the next installment, the excavated horse records offer another testable question: how did the station keep mounts ready for travelers and urgent messages? That question returns us to the workers and animals behind movement itself.
paragraphs.zh: 悬泉置因此以更尖锐的个案回答了居延留下的问题。登记与递送不只维持边塞驻地的供给，也让约定、申诉和调查得以在河西走廊各处追踪。有记录的链条并不保证公正，却让人们有途径质疑一种说法，让官员有办法索取证据。我们无需虚构有利的裁决，就能说明这一点。下一篇可以依出土的马匹文书追问另一个可核实的问题：驿站怎样让坐骑随时准备承载旅客与紧急文书？这会把我们带回支撑交通的劳作者与动物。

questions.q: What did the envoys allege about provisions and camel valuation?
questions.a: They alleged that promised provisions were missing and that officials undervalued the camels without their participation.

questions.q: What did the court ask Xuanquan to report?
questions.a: It asked for figures on provisions consumed by the Kangju party.

questions.q: Does the surviving record establish the final verdict?
questions.a: No. It documents an inquiry but not a final ruling or compensation.
